I'm all for gun rights, but I'm not convinced suppressors should be legal for hunting. Here's the best argument I could find, from the same website:

Most hunters do not wear not wear hearing protection in the field because they want to hear their surroundings. The trouble is, exposure to even a single unsuppressed gunshot can, and often does, lead to permanent hearing damage. Suppressors allow hunters to maintain full situational awareness, while still protecting their hearing. The result is a safer hunting experience for the hunter, and for those nearby.

(http://americansuppressorassociation.com/education/)

But I'm not convinced. As long as you aren't firing next to anyone's ear, guns aren't going to cause damage when fired outside. I just see it as a way to make it easier for the hunter to prevent all game from leaving the area, allowing them to take more shots. Have any more info on this?
I'll be honest, I'm not a hunter and can't give you much info on that aspect. I'm more interested in recreational target shooting without bothering my neighbors and minimizing hearing damage.

http://www.freehearingtest.com/hia_gunfirenoise.shtml

A .308 in a 24" barrel can instantly damage your hearing at 156.2 dB. Hearing loss is based on exposure time at a certain decibel level, 85~ dB is where city traffic is usually at, and you can listen to that for about eight hours before hearing loss begins to set in. Meanwhile a chainsaw's 115ish dB requires only a half a minute of exposure before you start to damage your hearing. Any time your ears ring, even a little bit, that means there's been damage and you have gotten slightly more deaf.

Gun shots are profoundly loud and even momentary exposure will wreck hearing.
